steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: : Human activities are increasing the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. The main greenhouse gases are carbon dioxide (CO₂) and methane (CH₄) . Water vapour is also a greenhouse gas. | : Increased greenhouse gas concentrations are causing global warming — an increase in the average temperature of the Earth. This leads to climate change , with significant consequences. | : A carbon footprint is the total amount of CO₂ and other greenhouse gas emissions caused by a person, organisation, event or product, expressed as a CO₂ equivalent. | : Reducing carbon footprints involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Methods include using renewable energy , improving energy efficiency , carbon capture , and changing agricultural practices .

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Name two greenhouse gases increased by human activity and state one source of each. | Describe three consequences of global warming / climate change. | Define the term "carbon footprint" and suggest two ways an individual could reduce their carbon footprint.
